Hi all,

Thanks — I reviewed the attached exhibit and annotated a few proposed edits (redlines_annotated.docx). Key commercial/legal points we propose:

1) Pen test / inspection rights
- Redwood can permit penetration testing subject to: (a) a defined test window with at least 14 calendar days' notice, (b) a scoped test plan (assets/IP ranges, test types) provided 7 days in advance, and (c) a Non-Disclosure and Rules of Engagement agreement.
- For production-facing tests, we propose a limited-scope approach: first attempt on staging, or production with strict blast-radius limits and rollback/kill-switch procedures.

2) Evidence / SOC 2 artifacts
- Redwood will provide an unredacted SOC 2 Type II report to the buyer under NDA and a quarterly attestation of controls changes.
- For operational evidence (logs, sampled traces), we propose a sampled/rolling cadence: Redwood will provide up to 3 sampled windows per 12-month period (each window up to 72 hours) with agreed selectors (request IDs, service components). This limits exposure while meeting audit needs.

3) Data handling and redaction
- Redwood will apply production-level redaction to PII before sharing. We also propose that any evidence shared remains subject to the buyer's confidentiality obligations and be destroyed after 90 days unless otherwise agreed.

4) Audit escalation path
- Add a 30-day remediation notice and opportunity to fix before escalation to formal inspection, and define SLAs for Redwood responses to evidence requests (10 business days for standard artifacts, expedited lanes for critical incidents).

If HealthGrid needs broader inspection rights, we can review but would expect additional contractual safeguards (scoped employee access, non-prod-first approach, support engineering on call).

Ben — can you confirm procurement's position on the 3-window proposal and whether that is likely to be acceptable?

Amelia — technical notes from the ops side:

- Evidence we can deliver: sampled request logs (application gateway + inference service), system-level audit logs (authN/authZ events), and config snapshots. We cannot export full production DBs or raw customer payloads without redaction.
- Retention & cadence: we recommend a rolling monthly evidence window (we can produce one sampled 72-hour window per month for up to three months on request) but will require selectors up front to locate relevant traces.
- Pen-test support: we can provide a staged test environment on short notice; for production tests we need a scheduled maintenance window and our SRE on call (we can provide 72-hour on-call coverage during the window).

Operational constraints to call out in contract language:
- Escalation SLA: Redwood will triage evidence requests within 48 business hours and provide an ETA for delivery.
- Cost: extended forensic work or ad hoc long-range log pulls are billable; we'll include a not-to-exceed hourly cap in the MAP to avoid surprises.

I'll prepare a short ops appendix to the exhibit that maps artifacts to selectors and timebox expectations. Sharing a draft link by EOD 5/18.
